newsitem.title: UK: WTO heading for new global trade round - UK's Lang.
newsitem.headline: WTO heading for new global trade round - UK's Lang.

text.p: The future work programme of the World Trade Organisation agreed last week means the WTO's 128 member countries are headed in effect for a new global round of trade talks, British Trade Secretary Ian Lang said on Tuesday.

Lang was reporting back to parliament on the results of last week's inaugural WTO ministerial conference in Singapore, which agreed among other things to establish working parties to explore the links between trade, investment and competition.
"We are already, from the agreement of this working programme, moving de facto towards a new trade round," Lang, who represented Britain at the conference, said.
"I would anticipate that at the next meeting of the WTO or the one after that it should be possible to achieve an absolute commitment to make further progress in this respect," he added.
The next ministerial conference will take place in Geneva in 1998.

Many countries are lukewarm about embarking on a full round of trade liberalisation talks so soon after the completion of the gruelling 1986-1993 Uruguay round, which freed up trade in goods, services, textiles and agriculture.
But Lang said: "There is a growing commitment within the WTO membership to recognise the benefits that trade liberalisation bring."
